opinions.reason: I attempted to falsify the artifact's two central claims (Defect A: cmd_tick/_arc_next_locked save first_issued without committing; Defect B: approve/reject take no tick_lock, PATCH-conditional on the POSIX wait bound) by independently re-checking roughly 70 of its path:line and quote citations against the actual repo at /home/user/chimera on main, and every one held exactly. I also independently recounted tests/test_g2_token.py: 14 test functions total, and reading each body confirms exactly the 7 the artifact names (lines 63,86,105,148,172,189,209) call approve/reject via CLI or gates.g2_approve, while the 3 the artifact names as not doing so (test_digest_is_not_a_credential:128, test_a_rotated_digest_is_trusted_only_once_committed:223, test_verify_operator_compares_in_constant_time:273) indeed only call gates.verify_operator directly -- the corrected-count claim in Open finding 1 is accurate and the prior 'eight' would have been wrong. I found no fabricated anchor, no misquote, and no place where the recommendation (PATCH classification, the two-line smallest fixes, the sequencing requirement to ship B's POSIX-wait bound before or with the lock) fails to follow from the cited evidence; the artifact's own self-disclosed limits (Defect B's git-index-lock behavior is asserted from git semantics with 'no git command was executed for this run', and the live arc-state.json line-drift) are honestly flagged rather than hidden. Given the volume and precision of confirming evidence and the absence of any contradicting fact after deliberately adversarial checking, I cannot construct a fatal or material refutation without hand-waving.

I checked ~35 of this artifact's highest-load-bearing citations against the actual repo state (not merely trusting the claims) and every one supported the claim exactly as stated: graph.py:545-550 (pending_calls stamps + 'Persisted by the caller' comment), graph.py:438 (bare write_text, no git), tests/test_no_write_outside_wrapper.py:13-18/28 (FORBIDDEN patterns + exact assert message), runner.py:9-11, cli.py:293-419 (the three pending_calls call sites and which ones checkpoint), gitio.py:79-114 (commit/push semantics, PERMANENT_PUSH_MARKERS, backoff tuple), queue.py:208-212/305-337/378-391/393-416 (_write, transition, record_approval, tick_lock, POSIX/Windows lock functions at 47-58 and 72-73), models.py:240, CHANGELOG.md:7-11 and :432-435, BACKLOG.md:597-603, TICK_PROTOCOL.md:4-27/89-102/172-174, gates.py:140-159/378-391, and graph.py:72/230-245/690-701 (CALL_CEILINGS, expired_labels, the halted-state branch). I independently re-derived the two most falsifiable meta-claims rather than trusting them: grepping every '.transition(' call site in src/ returned exactly cli.py:174,431,551,570 and gates.py:370,384,391 (matches the artifact's list precisely), and grepping tests/test_g2_token.py's 14 'def test_' lines plus every 'approve|reject' occurrence confirmed exactly the seven functions the artifact names (63,86,105,148,172,189,209) exercise approve/reject and the other seven do not — a claim precise enough that any drift would have been easy to catch, and there was none. I did not find a single load-bearing empirical claim lacking an in-tree citation, nor a citation that failed to support its claim. The only claims I could not independently verify are the raw test-execution outputs in the 'Test-surface baseline' section (427 passed in 15.29s, the 25 coverage-locating tests, gates.py exit 0) — I have no Bash access in this session to re-run them, but there is also no obvious in-tree authoritative source for ad-hoc run output to have been cited instead, so this is not a 'missing available source' defect, just an inherent limit of static review.
